topic: Why a shorter AS path can lose to a higher local preference.
goal: State the BGP best-path order and explain why local preference beats AS path length.
grill: I need to explain why traffic leaves through the longer AS path.
Two upstreams, one has a shorter path.
I think AS path length decides everything.

facts.claim: BGP compares weight, then local preference, then origin, then AS path length, then MED.
A route that arrives by eBGP has AS path length from the received path.
Local preference is compared before AS path length, so a longer path with a higher local preference wins.
facts.wrong: BGP always picks the route with the shortest AS path.

commandOutput: show bgp: path 65001 65002 local-pref 200 best; path 65003 local-pref 100 not best
